detail: Scenes 3 and 4 are the same surface with only a scroll between them — the rubric's explicit max-2 case. Their scene_N_page_text.json are byte-identical (6,948 chars, the SHP-2026-0202 modal), and the frames overlap by roughly half: scene 4 still shows the tail of scene 3's milestone rail (Kassala 0d vs plan, El Fasher +9d vs plan) and the same single-row Consignment lines table. Everything scene 4 adds is one card — an Event log containing exactly ONE entry: 'Jul 19, 2026 · Departed · Khartoum Central Warehouse · — · Phone check-in'. The claim it is asked to carry is the strongest invariant in the product ('status is derived from an append-only log, there is no cell to change before a Monday meeting'), and a one-line log cannot show a status being ADDED UP from anything. This is the sagging beat of the run: the frame is 50% recycled and the 50% that is new is the thinnest artifact in eight scenes.
fix_recommendation: Give scene 4 a log worth looking at and a reason to be its own frame. Seed SHP-2026-0202 with the full event chain it must have had (despatch from Khartoum, the Kassala arrival that stamped an actual, the re-estimate that produced the +9d) so the Event log renders four or five rows with differing SOURCE badges, and re-point the scene's final scroll so the milestone rail is OUT of frame and the log fills it. If the seed data cannot support that, merge scenes 3 and 4 into one beat and reclaim the runtime — one modal deserves one scene.

detail: Scene 6 is the scene whose removal would not be noticed. Its scripted payoff is the 'Weeks of cover' card giving the date each node runs dry — but scene 5's captured frame ALREADY contains that card (Biu / Damaturu / Dori / El Fasher, weekly burn, 'Not yet served', 'awaiting first consignment'), because scene 5 ends scrolled to the Kassala row with the cover table directly beneath it. Scene 6's own frame instead shows the exception column scene 1 already showed — the same Late / Expiry risk / Short receipt cards — plus the same grey 'Map unavailable' panel, with two italic lines of derivation ('How this was ranked: 9 days late against 0.0 weeks of cover; the days after the store runs dry x the admission rate') as its entire net contribution. Scenes 6 and 7 additionally have byte-identical page_text (6,119 chars) — a second same-surface-with-a-scroll pair. So the two scenes traded artifacts: 5 shows 6's payoff, 6 shows 1's queue.
fix_recommendation: Stop scene 5 at the coverage table (scroll to Kassala but hold ABOVE the cover card, or collapse it) so the Weeks-of-cover reveal is still unspent, and make scene 6 open on that card with the projected run-dry dates as its subject, expanding one exception's derivation over it. Alternatively cut scene 6 outright and move its one line of derivation onto scene 1's opening row — the queue-ranking claim is already made there.

detail: This is a NARRATIVE choice, not a product limitation — the product demonstrably has other surfaces. Frames 1, 6, 7 and 8 are the same exception-card column in the same left panel at four scroll offsets; frames 3 and 4 are the same consignment modal at two. Only scene 3 (a milestone timeline rail, genuinely not a table) and scene 5 (dense caseload/coverage + weeks-of-cover tables with IPC badges) break the pattern. Worse, the one shape the narrative itself describes at length — the reallocation modal in scene 8, with the constrained list of nodes genuinely holding surplus, what each can spare without dropping below its own threshold, and the required reason textarea — is executed by the actions (fill + click + wait_for .toast) but never captured. Across eight frames the viewer never sees a decision BEING MADE, only its record. The product's most differentiated interaction is invisible in the run.
fix_recommendation: Split scene 8 into a capture on the OPEN reallocation modal (source list, spare-capacity figures, the typed reason) and a capture on the closed row, or add a hold + snapshot between the fill and the Reallocate click. That converts the run's fourth exception-column frame into its only form frame and costs nothing narratively — the modal is already opened by the existing actions.

detail: The Network panel renders as a grey box reading 'Map unavailable — This environment has no Mapbox access token configured, so the network map cannot be drawn' in frames 1, 6, 7 and 8, where it occupies roughly 45% of the viewport. The recipe acknowledges this ('renders blank without a Mapbox token') and works around it in scene 2, but the workaround does not help the four frames that keep it on screen — including the OPENING frame, where the first thing a viewer's eye lands on beside the headline is a configuration error. It is also the surface that would have supplied the run's missing shape contrast: a corridor map is the one non-table, non-list thing the narrative promises and never delivers.
fix_recommendation: Set a Mapbox token in the walkthrough capture environment (the runner page already provides MAPBOX_TOKEN elsewhere in this repo, and the WebGL patch for headless capture is documented) so the corridor map draws in the four frames that already frame it. If a token cannot be provisioned for capture, collapse or hide the Network card when no token is present so the frames show a full-width queue instead of a half-frame apology.

detail: Eight frames carry the header chip 'Procurement · Ada Nwosu', and the narration for scene 8 is 'Ada answers the shortfall Komadugu raised', with the concept claim resting on the record 'carrying the actor and the recorded reason'. The line the frame actually renders is 'Closed by oes-lead@oes.example on Jul 28, 2026, against the reallocation that answered it.' At the one moment the demo asks the viewer to read who decided, the named person the whole story follows resolves to a generic role address. Everything else about the persona is clean — one actor, one goal, no handoff — which is why this single string is disproportionately costly.
fix_recommendation: Stamp the SupplyAction actor with the persona's display name (and, if the model keeps an account, render 'Ada Nwosu (oes-lead@oes.example)') so the closed row names the person the narration names. Seed-data or serializer change; no narrative rework needed.

detail: The opening leads on one number — '2,428 Children at risk / across 8 unanswered exceptions' — and scene 8's narration promises 'the headline stops counting its eighty-seven children'. The state change is REAL: scene 8's page text reads '2,341 / across 7 unanswered exceptions · 1 closed', exactly 87 fewer, against 2,428 in both scene 1 and scene 7. But scene 8's captured frame begins mid-list (top of frame is the tail of a Djibo late card) and the KPI row is off-screen, so the run's single cleanest numeric proof — the opening's own headline decrementing by the exact figure the finale claims — is never shown. The queue-sink IS visible (a Monguno short-receipt card sits below the Askira row in scene 7 and nothing but the Pipeline card sits below it in scene 8), so the loop closes; it just closes without its best evidence in frame.
fix_recommendation: After the reallocation toast, add a scroll to the KPI row and a short hold so the frame carries '2,341 · across 7 unanswered exceptions · 1 closed' with the closed row beneath it — or capture a second frame for scene 8 at the top of the page. Ideally the final frame contains both the changed headline and the closed row, which is the entire before/after the narration is describing.

detail: Scene 2's job in the sequence is to establish the honesty gradient — EPCIS from the Kano plant, a despatch advice from Lagos, a driver's phone check-in on the Port Sudan leg — so that later scenes can trade on 'the picture is brightest where access is easiest'. The captured frame's REPORTED BY column reads 'Phone check-in' on all four consignment rows, and the page text contains zero occurrences of 'EPCIS' and no despatch-advice badge (the phrase appears twice, only as prose). A gradient shown at one point is not a gradient, so the chapter opens weaker than the beats that depend on it. Scoring note: this is a sequence-level consequence, not a re-score of the concept judge's per-scene claim/frame check.
fix_recommendation: Point scene 2 at a contract or a delivery-schedule view whose rows span all three tiers (a Nigeria corridor with Kano EPCIS rows beside the Sudan phone check-ins), so the three badges appear side by side in one frame. If no single contract spans them, use the corridor pipeline table where several contracts are listed together.
